title: NEMPAL SINGH versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
(Before the National Lok Adalat)
THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE SIDDHARTHA SAH
12TH SEPTEMBER, 2026
Criminal Misc. Application U/s 528 No.1485 of 2026
Nempal Singh .....Applicant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and another .....Respondents
Presence:-
Counsel for the applicant : Mr. Avidit Noliyal, Advocate.
Counsel for State : Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned AGA
Counsel for Respondent no.2 : Mr. Harshit Deopa, Advocate
holding brief of Mr. Vishal
Vikram Singh, Advocate.
Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
By means of the present application under Section
528 of BNSS, 2023, the applicant has sought to quash the
entire criminal proceedings in relationship of the
compromise entered between the parties and to quash the
FIR No.85 of 2025, Police Station Gadarpur, District Udham
Singh Nagar, charge-sheet dated 17.05.2025, under
Sections 115(2), 352 of BNS, 2023 and 3(1)(r) SC/ST Act
and cognizance/summoning order dated 10.02.2026, under
Sections 115(2), 352 of BNS, 2023 and 3(1)(r) SC/ST Act,
pending in the court of learned Special Sessions Judge,
Udham Singh Nagar (Rudrapur) in Special Sessions Trial
No.86 of 2026, State of Uttarakhand vs. Nempal Singh.

2
2. The compounding application has been filed. The
affidavit in support of the compounding application has been
filed on behalf of respondent no.2 and the Court also
interacted with respondent no.2-Mr. Budh Dev through V.C.
he states that he does not want to prosecute the applicant
any further and the matter has been settled between the
parties. The written compromise between the parties is
already on record.
3. Mr. Nempal Singh is present in person duly
identified by Mr. Avidit Noliyal, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Budh Dev is present through V.C. duly identified by Mr.
Harshit Deopa, Advocate for respondent no.2.
4. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned AGA for the State
would submit that since Section 3(1)(r) SC/ST Act is non-compoundable, the matter is not compoundable. However,
since parties have entered into a settlement, the respondent
no.2 does not want to prosecute the applicant any further,
in such view of the matter, letting the matter go into trial it
would be a futile exercise, therefore, the compounding
application deserves to be allowed.
5. Also, in view of the law laid down by Hon'ble the
Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab,
2012 (10) SCC 303, Dimpey Gujral vs. Union Territory,
Chandigarh, (2013) 11 SCC 497, B.S. Joshi vs. State of

3
Haryana, (2003) 4 SCC 675, Nikhil Merchant vs. CBI, (2008)
9 SCC 677, the objection of the learned AGA does not
sustain.
6. The present the Compounding Application
(Compromise Application) is hereby allowed. The offences
are permitted to be compounded. The entire criminal
proceedings in pursuance to FIR No.85 of 2025, Police
Station Gadarpur, District Udham Singh Nagar, charge-sheet
dated 17.05.2025, under Sections 115(2), 352 of BNS,
2023 and 3(1)(r) SC/ST Act and cognizance/summoning
order dated 10.02.2026, under Sections 115(2), 352 of
BNS, 2023 and 3(1)(r) SC/ST Act, pending in the court of
learned Special Session Judge, Udham Singh Nagar
(Rudrapur) in Special Session Trial No.86 of 2026, State of
Uttarakhand vs. Nempal Singh, are hereby quashed.
7. The C528 application is, accordingly, disposed of.
8. All pending applications, if any, stand disposed of
accordingly.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.)
Dated : 12th September, 2026
Ravi
